precepts.text: Enter not into the path of the wicked; they sleep not except they have done mischief, and they drink the wine of violence.
precepts.point: Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil. Enter not into the path of the wicked; sinners entice, saying come with us, cast in thy lot among us, but walk not thou in the way with them, for their feet run to evil and make haste to shed blood. Many of our young men's lives end short because they follow a multitude to do evil. To be in the midst of the singing, like the whole school hollering fight, fight, fight, is to be in the multitude the Most High warns of; a soul without knowledge of the laws of God hastes with his feet and sins.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil”. Proverbs says the same: “Enter not into the path of the wicked, and go not in the way of evil men. Avoid it, pass not by it, turn from it, and pass away.”

Why: “For they sleep not, except they have done mischief; and their sleep is taken away, unless they cause some to fall. For they eat the bread of wickedness, and drink the wine of violence.” The multitude that does evil cannot rest until it has done mischief and caused some to fall. Do not go in the way with them.

precepts.text: For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law; the doctrine is the law.
precepts.point: Going contrary to the laws of marriage, of the sabbath, of raising children righteously, or of going to thy brother alone when there is an ought between you, and secretly enticing others to follow, is how one turns people away from the Lord; those men and those women have to be put out from among the body.

note.label: Deuteronomy 13: Enticers to Other Gods Put Away

precepts.why:
“For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law.” The doctrine which ye have learned, the doctrine that divisions and offences are marked against, is the law. Good doctrine and the law are one and the same: forsake ye not my law.

So the one who causes divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine is the one going contrary to the laws: of marriage, of the sabbath, of raising children righteously, of going to thy brother alone when there is an ought between you. To speak to turn people away from the Lord their God is to speak against his law, and it is out of the way of that law that the deceiver thrusts them.

precepts.text: Take fast hold of instruction and avoid the path of the wicked, for they sleep not unless they cause some to fall.
precepts.point: Day and night they go about seeking violence; wickedness is in the midst and deceit and guile depart not from her streets.

note.label: Psalm 55: Cast Thy Burden Upon the Lord

precepts.why:
“Take fast hold of instruction; let her not go: keep her; for she is thy life. Enter not into the path of the wicked, and go not in the way of evil men. Avoid it, pass not by it, turn from it, and pass away.” In a city full of violence and strife, take fast hold of instruction and avoid the path of the wicked altogether.

“For they sleep not, except they have done mischief; and their sleep is taken away, unless they cause some to fall.” That is why day and night they go about it upon the walls: they cannot sleep unless they have done mischief and caused some to fall. Instruction is thy life; hold it fast and turn from their way.

precepts.text: For their feet run to evil and make haste to shed blood, the same wicked path Solomon says to avoid and turn from.
precepts.point: The path of the just is as the shining light that shineth more and more unto the perfect day, but the way of the wicked is as darkness; they know not at what they stumble.

note.label: Proverbs 4: Wisdom Is the Principal Thing

precepts.why:
“Enter not into the path of the wicked, and go not in the way of evil men. Avoid it, pass not by it, turn from it, and pass away.” This is the same thing we read in Proverbs 1: “For their feet run to evil, and make haste to shed blood.”

The path of the wicked is the path of feet that run to evil and make haste to shed blood. That is why the warning is so full: avoid it, pass not by it, turn from it, pass away. These are the men who sleep not except they have done mischief, who eat the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of violence.

Their way is darkness and they know not at what they stumble, but the path of the just is the shining light unto the perfect day. Turn from the one and walk in the other.

precepts.text: The good doctrine is His law, which He tells us not to forsake, so all denominations and philosophies are set aside for it.
precepts.point: The prophets spoke in similitudes, so not everyone will understand; the Most High shows His secrets through precepts, line upon line, a little here and a little there, to those He chooses to teach.

note.label: Song of Solomon 8: Love Strong as Death, the Vineyard of Israel

precepts.why:
What is the doctrine he teaches those weaned from the milk? “For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law.” The good doctrine is his law, which he tells us not to forsake.

So all denominations and philosophies are set aside for it. The understanding the breasts stand for is understanding of the law.

precepts.text: The Most High gives good doctrine; the doctrine to be understood is the law.
precepts.point: With stammering lips and another tongue He will speak to this people; off the slave ships Israel spoke different languages, and because they did not keep the law the oppressor's culture was beaten into them until they came to understand. This Bible is the rest and the refreshing, yet they would not hear, so the word came precept upon precept that they might fall backward and be broken and snared.

note.label: Isaiah 28: Woe to the Drunkards of Ephraim and Precept Upon Precept

precepts.why:
“Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand doctrine?” Solomon shows what that doctrine is: “For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law.” The good doctrine the Most High gives is his law. So the doctrine to be understood in Isaiah 28 is the law of God, and the ones he teaches it to are “them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts.”

That is why the method is “precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little”. A scripture must be laid upon another scripture. The Bible is a puzzle, in the Old and New Testaments, that must be unfolded and put together, and put together along with keeping God’s laws, because the doctrine and the law are one and the same.

precepts.text: For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law; the doctrines are the laws.
precepts.point: The waters that issue out from under the threshold are the word of the Most High. Just as a tub fills when the water is left running, the word is now being issued out to the four corners of the earth.

note.label: Ezekiel 47: The Waters Issuing from the House

precepts.why:
“For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law.” The doctrines are the laws. Good doctrine and the law are the same thing in the same breath.

So when Moses says his doctrine shall drop as the rain, and the water issuing from the house is the word, that water is the law of the Most High. The word going out from the spiritual house of Israel to the four corners of the earth is His good doctrine, His law, and we are not to forsake it.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 15 The Seven Last Plagues

precepts.why: What is God’s doctrine? “For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law.” The law is his doctrine. What is the true religion? The law. What is the true doctrine? The law.

points: Get wisdom, get understanding, forget it not, neither decline from the words of my mouth. Decline means to pull back. We have brothers and sisters who have declined, taken their hand off the plow; they were introduced to the mighty heritage, you are the Israelites, the sons of God, and then the cares of this world and the lust of the flesh took them out of here. That is when you hear the complaints: I am overwhelmed, cap. There is no better place to be overwhelmed than for the Lord; you would rather be overwhelmed for your nine to five, invest more in this world than in the Lord? Overwhelmed from editing videos to wake up your people, from traveling, from teaching brothers who are brand new? That is a shame.
Neither decline from the words of my mouth: the mouth of God is this Bible. But who is he using to edify the people and the nation?
